messages.1. 先看原文，再选类型\n“姓名”是说话的人，“正文”是他说的话，“选项”是菜:
1. Read the samples, then choose a role
"Name" is the speaker, "Message" is their dialogue, and "Choice" is menu text. "Ignore" excludes the text. "Auto" lets the tool decide.

2. Colors link messages to names
Within one function, a blue message belongs to the blue name and a red message belongs to the red name. Colors identify groups, not characters. Automatic colors are assigned only when a name is present. Messages without a name default to "None" and are exported separately.

3. Click the color dot or "None" beside a role to change the pairing
Choose "Pair with name" for the matching speaker. Choose "None" to export the item separately. Different names need different colors; use "New pairing group" to create another group. Choices and ignored text do not need names.

4. One name can have several messages
If a name and two messages share blue, two records are exported, each with that name and one message. Translate repeated instances of the same name consistently to avoid conflicts during import.

5. Unmatched items trigger a warning
If a name has no message, you can edit the pairing or export the name alone. Two names cannot share a color; change one of their groups first.

6. Choices and prompts are included by default
Choices in Select functions are included automatically. Menu prompts (outline) are exported as separate messages. Choose "Ignore" to exclude text, or uncheck the function to exclude it entirely. Source text containing only ASCII letters, numbers and symbols is skipped; translations have no such restriction.

7. No need to scan every time
Scan results are saved and reused when you reopen the page. Click "Rescan" to update them. "Show all functions" also lists functions without extractable text. Search and "Enabled only" work together without rescanning.

Export: select ScenarioDB / StringsDB extracted from an ARC archive, or their directory. JSON uses UTF-8 and can be edited in a text editor.

Rebuild: the database type is read from JSON. Single files default to .rebuilt; batch processing restores original names for repacking with the archive tool.

Verify: decode binary to JSON, rebuild and compare byte for byte without writing files.

Binary strings use CP932. ScenarioDB automatically detects 64-byte and 128-byte records. The 64-byte format stores only label (up to 63 bytes). The 128-byte format stores resource (up to 95 bytes) and label (up to 31 bytes). In the 64-byte format, record order determines resource names such as Scenario0000; preserve that order and the record_size field in JSON. StringsDB allows up to 27 bytes for text. Limits apply to encoded bytes. Overlong or unencodable text causes an error.

ScenarioDB supports up to 1024 records; StringsDB up to 8192. The four key components, duplicate IDs and record order are preserved. Unknown nonzero padding causes an error to prevent data loss.

Existing output is not overwritten by default. Individual failures are logged, and batch processing continues.
